dedupe_keys.name: life at the fenceline interactive map and report on people living near high risk chemical facilities ejha 2018

description: Life at the Fenceline is an interactive map and report showing who lives within a three-mile fenceline zone of the almost 12,500 high-risk chemical facilities in the United States, which pose a constant threat of catastrophic explosion or poison gas release. The analysis found that 124 million Americans, 39% of the population, live in such zones, as do 24 million children at 125,000 schools and 11,000 medical facilities, and that residents are disproportionately people of colour and poor and face higher cancer and respiratory risk from air pollution; nine environmental justice communities are examined in more depth. It was produced by the Environmental Justice Health Alliance for Chemical Policy Reform (EJHA) and released with Coming Clean on 26 September 2018. Coverage is national for the US. The map is free online as an ArcGIS web map and the report is a free PDF. Caveats: it is an advocacy analysis from 2018, facility lists and zones may have changed since, and no data licence or download is given. For simulation it shows how many people, schools and hospitals lie in chemical accident exposure zones, useful for hazard exposure and emergency response planning around industrial sites. It is related to the CSB recommendations database record in this catalogue.
